transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-24 11:00 PDT / 18:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Rahul Desai (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (BlueHarbor Platform Lead), Marcus Boyd (BlueHarbor Head Infra), Evelyn Li (BlueHarbor FinOps), Danny Wu (BlueHarbor Product)

[00:00:00] Lena (Redwood): hey everybody thanks for making time, quick rollout of agenda — console walk, per-route cost, and then Q&A.
[00:00:12] Priya: yep thank you, we've got Evelyn and Marcus on, we'll be taking notes for FinOps and infra.
[00:00:20] Rahul (Redwood): alright i'm going to share screen, give me one sec — screen is up?
[00:00:30] Speaker 1: yep visible.
[00:00:34] Rahul: cool okay so first slide is the usage map, this is a synthetic demo org but the UI and drilldowns are identical to what you get in the console. you can see routes on the left, aggregated tokens and cost middle, and SLO markers on the right.
[00:00:55] Marcus: quick question — what do you consider a route? is that endpoint path or product feature?
[00:01:02] Rahul: good Q. route is defined by your routing tag — so it's often endpoint path + model id + environment. lots of customers tag by feature (search, summarization, chat) and we surface them as discrete routes. sometimes the transcription shows K-V cash instead of cache, sorry for the shorthand.
[00:01:20] Priya: ok so if we have a single `/generate` endpoint used by both mobile and web, we can create two routes by tagging?
[00:01:28] Lena: exactly — you can apply runtime tags at the SDK/client layer or in the gateway. we also support auto-inferred routes from path + query when you don't tag explicitly, but tagging gives you precise chargeback.
[00:01:45] [00:02:00] Rahul: zooming into the route view — here's per-route latency distribution, cost per 1k tokens, and model mix. notice the modal on the right showing model variants and quantization recommendations.
[00:02:12] Evelyn: cost per 1k tokens — is that normalized across models or raw?
[00:02:18] Rahul: it's normalized by compute-equivalent tokens and includes our cost model — so we convert tokens into vcompute-units, then map to GPU profile. in practice you can toggle "raw token" or "cost-normalized". the default is cost-normalized so finance teams get an apples-to-apples view.
[00:02:42] Marcus: are those vcompute estimates derived from your runtime telemetry or from a static lookup table?
[00:02:48] Rahul: runtime telemetry + model profile. we run micro-benchmarks per model shape and sequence length distributions, then the console shows empirical per-token cost adjusted by your observed latency/batching. it's not just a static CSV.
[00:03:02] [00:03:30] Rahul: here's the breakdown panel — tokens, compute, infra (cloud/GPU), and add-ons like storage for KV cache. you can expand the infra row to see region-level pricing.
[00:03:45] Priya: storage for KV cache — can you exclude that from route cost? some of our routes use a shared KV cache across features.
[00:03:52] Rahul: yes you can attribute cache to routes via scoping rules, or mark it as shared infra in the chargeback view. in the exports we provide both per-route attributed and shared-pool views.
[00:04:10] [00:04:40] Lena: quick pause — i'll call out a note on private/dedicated. some customers want identical console UX while routing private traffic to their VPC/dedicated pool. we support that and you still get the same per-route dashboards and exports.
[00:04:58] Marcus: any constraints for private? network egress or KMS access?
[00:05:03] Lena: you keep control — KMS integrations and HSM are supported, and we can operate over an expresslink or private peering. there are config items we'll share in the Private deployment checklist.
[00:05:20] [00:05:45] Rahul: now a feature I want to show — the route-level cost rollup with rules engine. you can write mapping rules like: if tag.environment == "prod" and route contains "/search" then map to cost center X, apply 10% overhead, and set billable owner to team-search. the UI gives instant previews of the mapping on the last 30 days.
[00:06:06] Danny (Customer): can mapping rules be done via API as code? we prefer infra-as-code.
[00:06:12] Rahul: yes — full API and Terraform provider support. mappings are stored as JSON, but we have a gui editor for quick ops.
[00:06:25] [00:06:50] Evelyn: on the billing export — what format? CSV only? a flat file?
[00:06:56] Rahul: CSV and parquet. the export includes route_id, tags, model_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, compute_units, cost, and line-item breakdown for infra. we also have a GL-ready chargeback export for accounting systems.
[00:07:20] Priya: is there an example we can look at?
[00:07:24] Lena: yes we'll attach a sample export in the follow-up. Rahul has a demo export he can pull now.
[00:07:30] [00:07:45] Rahul: pulling the export — ok here's a sample of last 7 days. note the top 5 routes by cost, and you can click any to get request-level drilldown with anonymized prompt hashes (for privacy).
[00:08:05] Marcus: prompt hashes are anonymized, we don't send prompt content to Redwood?
[00:08:11] Rahul: by default we store metadata only; for hosted customers you can opt-in to content logging for debugging but there's an off-by-default policy and redaction tools. for Private setups you can keep logs in your VPC.
[00:08:30] [00:09:00] Speaker 2 (Priya): okay can you show that cost waterfall again? the compute vs infra split especially.
[00:09:05] Rahul: sure — waterfall expands: model compute, GPU infra, storage & cache, network egress, and add-ons. we also show the impact of batching and prefix cache on the same view.
[00:09:30] Rahul: here's an interactive toggle — if you enable prefix caching for a route you'll see cost drop simulation immediately. for example route /summaries-quick shows a 42% token cost reduction when cached with a 90% hit rate.
[00:09:52] Evelyn: that simulation assumes no change in latency?
[00:09:56] Rahul: usually latency improves since fewer decoder steps occur, but some cache retrieval adds a small lookup latency; the console models both and surfaces an expected p50/p95 change.
[00:10:12] [00:10:40] Marcus: how do you handle model rollouts? if we want to A/B a quantized model to save costs, can we compare routes side by side?
[00:10:48] Rahul: yes — rollouts show per-route model variant split, quality regression alerts tied to evals, and you can set automatic fallback to a higher-fidelity model if certain thresholds fail. we also show projected cost savings.
[00:11:10] [00:11:30] Priya: our SLO is p95 < 350ms for critical routes and cost per 1k tokens under $X — can console enforce routing policies to favor low-latency pool when before cost pool?
[00:11:42] Lena: you can define routing policies by priority — latency-first, cost-first, or hybrid. policies can be per-route and have fallback chains.
[00:11:56] [00:12:20] Rahul: small note — the latency metrics are from real requests annotated with model variant and pool id, so you can do root cause analysis: is latency from model selection, network, or queuing.
[00:12:36] Marcus: is there tracing integration? X-Ray, Jaeger?
[00:12:40] Rahul: yes we integrate with OpenTelemetry, and we can forward spans to your tracing backend.
[00:12:55] [00:13:20] Danny: competitor question — how do you compare to InferOps on cost visibility? they have decent dashboards.
[00:13:27] Lena: InferOps focuses on self-hosted runtime metrics; Redwood combines runtime economics with a curated model catalog and routing policies, plus hosted + private options. we emphasize per-route chargeback and the export formats finance teams need.
[00:13:50] [00:14:10] Priya: any red flags on our side — we run on multi-cloud and have regional residency requirements for EU.
[00:14:18] Lena: that's supported — region-level pricing and routing by region, and you can restrict data residency on a per-customer basis with Private deployment. we'll share the compliance pack.
[00:14:35] [00:15:00] Rahul: demoing alerts now — you can create a cost anomaly alert for a route when daily spend deviates by X sigma, and we link anomalies back to request samples for investigation.
[00:15:18] Evelyn: can alerts create PagerDuty incidents?
[00:15:22] Rahul: yep, webhooks, PagerDuty, Slack.
[00:15:40] [00:16:05] Priya: about chargeback rules — can we apply hard overrides for internal showback vs external billing?
[00:16:12] Rahul: you can. multiple export views exist: internal showback (with overhead and shared infra splits), and customer-facing billing lines that flatten overhead into the route cost.
[00:16:30] [00:16:55] Danny: is there sample code for tagging from mobile clients? we worry about token size and SDK weight.
[00:17:02] Rahul: yes — lightweight header-based tagging is our recommended pattern. we'll share sample SDK snippets for iOS/Android and server-side proxies.
[00:17:25] [00:17:50] Marcus: curious about unit economics — if we quantize GPT-style models and move to ded. pool, what's the expected capex vs opex tradeoff?
[00:17:58] Lena: that depends on utilization. Redwood Optimize can run suggestions — for example for long-tail routes with low QPS we recommend quantized models on cheaper GPUs; for hot routes we suggest dedicated pools with autoscaling. in general Dedicated reduces unit cost at high sustained throughput.
[00:18:25] Rahul: i'll show a sample Optimize recommendation — it suggests a model switch and projects a 28% cost reduction with <1% quality delta based on evals.
[00:18:40] [00:19:05] Priya: how do we validate quality regressions? we have a set of prompts we care about.
[00:19:11] Rahul: bring your prompt set — we can run closed-loop evals and produce a regression report. the console ties regressions to routes and can trigger automatic rollback.
[00:19:30] [00:19:55] Lena: quick recap — we showed route dashboards, mapping rules, exports, alerts, and Optimize suggestions. open floor for final Qs.
[00:20:10] Evelyn: on security docs — can you attach SOC2 and ISO?
[00:20:15] Maya (Redwood CSM): yes we will share the security pack after this meeting, plus the private deployment checklist.
[00:20:28] Priya: what's the typical onboarding timeline for a pilot?
[00:20:33] Lena: pilot can be as short as two weeks for a scoped route set — most run 4–8 weeks to gather statistically significant cost & quality data.
[00:20:44] Marcus: what's required on our side to start?
[00:20:48] Lena: access to a billing export, a list of routes with tags (or we'll help infer), and an API key with a sandbox org. for Private we need network peering setup and KMS details.
[00:21:05] [00:21:25] Rahul: i'll show a final ex- export for accounting teams — the GL-ready view maps to cost centers and has a reconciliation column.
[00:21:40] Danny: can that reconcile to Snowflake or our data warehouse?
[00:21:44] Rahul: you can push parquet to S3 and load to Snowflake; we also have connectors in preview.
[00:21:58] [00:22:20] Priya: ok let's talk next steps — Evelyn will share billing data, we'll get the pricing sheet, and then schedule pilot kickoff.
[00:22:30] Lena: perfect. we'll send the follow-up email with artifacts: pricing spreadsheet, sample export, tagging guide, security pack, and a 5-min console screencap.
[00:22:45] Evelyn: sounds good, thanks.
[00:22:50] Marcus: thanks everyone.
[00:22:55] Lena: thanks, we'll follow up.
[00:23:00] [END] 

Notes on transcript quality: medium — some speaker labels generic, a few words mis-transcribed (K-V cash, sock two), timestamps approximate.
